# Product Backlog

Product Goal, Now / Next / Later, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-09-16:

> **Now:** The freelancers and small practices Sam and Lee bring in
> personally run their real invoicing on Acme and pay for it. Measured as
> practices sending real invoices, first paid purchases, and a written reason
> from everyone who declines.
>
> **Next:** Strangers find and pay for Acme without a personal introduction.
> Measured as paying customers from ads, search, and from invoices existing
> users send.
>
> **Later:** Solo professionals treat Acme as the way finished work becomes
> confirmed payment, and the business sustains itself from revenue.

Previous goal (superseded 2026-09-16): accepted 2026-07-10, it framed the
Product Goal as reaching first-paid-traffic readiness — a reliable, simple,
delightful MVP letting a new sole proprietor or freelancer create and send a
trackable invoice without account friction, giving the client a clear path to
pay, and measuring the core journey well enough to spend the first €100 on
qualified traffic and judge whether real users want Acme.

Backlog items are ordered by their contribution to the Product Goal.

This table is ordered from highest priority to lowest priority.
Per the Scrum Guide shape used in Gnomik, the active Product Backlog is the ordered list of work still needed to improve the product; completed items stay out of the active order.

The backlog is flat: each PBI is a complete, independently acceptable outcome.
There are no parent/child PBIs or partial-PBI Sprint selections. The Product
Owner may reshape, merge, replace, or reorder items as learning changes the work.

> [!info] Working agreement: one PBI in progress at a time (PO-approved 2026-09-17)
> The team works one backlog item that serves the Sprint Goal and pulls the next only after that item is merged, deployed, live-proven and reported for PO review, or is parked as Waiting with its external condition and watcher named (see the `Waiting` status below). Subagents parallelize packets inside one PBI, never across PBIs. Shape PBIs so acceptance is within the team's control; move outcome evaluation into its own item (example: PBI-014 (Run and evaluate the first €100 viability test) follows PBI-013 (Pass the first-paid-traffic readiness gate)). Full wording also recorded in `AGENTS.md` Product Owner Standing Directives.

> [!info] Status legend
> `Proposed` (not yet ordered by the Product Owner) · `Ready` (refined, sized, may be pulled into a Sprint when capacity frees) · `Planned` (Product Owner decision 2026-09-24: Sprint-bound only — taken into the active Sprint, or reserved for the upcoming one — carries a "Sprint:" tag, e.g. "Sprint: S9") · `Conditional` (Product Owner decision 2026-09-24: ready when its named precondition lands; not in a Sprint) / `Blocked` (unselected, waiting on a precondition or later trigger) · `Selected` (chosen for a Sprint, work not yet started) · `In Progress` (Product Owner decision 2026-09-24: active work within the Sprint — carries a "Sprint:" tag, e.g. "Sprint: S8"; single spelling, only PBI-051 (Acme Invoice Admin Page) holds this status) · `Waiting` (the team is not working on it; done-ness depends on an external result — campaign data, PO action, third party — with the wait condition named in the row) · `Ready for Product Owner review` (released, awaiting sign-off) · `Done` (whole-item Product Owner acceptance) · `Cancelled` (Product Owner stopped the item) · `Pending PBR` (back in the Product Backlog, not sprintable until refined at Product Backlog Refinement).
>
> **Priority order (Product Owner decision 2026-09-24):** the priority number is not an element of the PBI card — it is a place at which any PBI could be placed. The team works only on the highest-priority items; this table's document order is priority order. `Planned`/`In Progress` status plus the `Sprint:` tag are the source of truth for what is in a Sprint.
